text: The Economic Survey 2025-26 was tabled in Parliament on:
explanation:
• It was tabled on 29 January 2026.
  • Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman placed it in Parliament.
  • The Union Budget 2026-27 followed on 1 February 2026.
  • The Survey is the yearly report card of the economy.
subject: gk

text: The Economic Survey 2025-26 was prepared under which Chief Economic Adviser?
explanation:
• CEA V. Anantha Nageswaran led the Survey.
  • It is drafted by the Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs.
  • The CEA works in the Ministry of Finance.
  • Arvind Subramanian and K. Subramanian were earlier CEAs.

text: Which body prepares the Economic Survey of India?
option_D: Economic Division, Department of Economic Affairs
explanation:
• The Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs prepares it.
  • The department is part of the Ministry of Finance.
  • The Chief Economic Adviser heads the work.
  • The first Survey was presented for 1950-51.

text: How many chapters does the Economic Survey 2025-26 have?
explanation:
• The Survey has 16 chapters.
  • It runs to about 739 pages in one volume.
  • A short chart-based 'Highlights' booklet came with it.
  • Its closing chapter deals with Swadeshi and strategic indispensability.

text: As per the First Advance Estimates cited in the Economic Survey 2025-26, India's real GDP growth for FY26 is:
explanation:
• Real GDP growth for FY26 is put at 7.4%.
  • Real GVA is estimated to grow 7.3%.
  • India stayed the fastest-growing major economy for a fourth year.
  • Advance estimates are released by the NSO under MoSPI.
subject: gk

text: The Economic Survey 2025-26 projects India's real GDP growth for FY27 in the range of:
explanation:
• The FY27 projection is 6.8% to 7.2%.
  • FY26 growth is estimated at 7.4%.
  • Domestic demand is the main support for growth.
  • The previous Survey had projected 6.3%–6.8% for FY26.
subject: gk

text: India's potential growth rate, as assessed in the Economic Survey 2025-26, is about:
explanation:
• Potential growth was raised to about 7%.
  • Reforms, capex and productivity gains support it.
  • Potential growth is the rate an economy can sustain without overheating.
  • FY27 growth is projected at 6.8%–7.2%.

text: Real Gross Value Added (GVA) growth for FY26 is estimated in the Survey at:
explanation:
• Real GVA growth is estimated at 7.3%.
  • Real GDP growth is 7.4%.
  • GDP = GVA + product taxes − product subsidies.
  • Services are estimated to grow about 9.1%.
subject: gk

text: Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE) as a share of GDP in FY26 reached:
explanation:
• PFCE reached 61.5% of GDP.
  • This is the highest share since 2012; FY23 had the same level.
  • PFCE grew 7.0% in FY26.
  • Low inflation and steady jobs supported spending.
subject: gk

text: In the FY26 advance estimates, the services sector's share in GVA touched a record of:
explanation:
• Services reached a record 56.4% of GVA.
  • Services were 53.6% of GDP in H1 FY26.
  • Services growth is estimated at about 9.1% for FY26.
  • Services drew about 80% of FDI inflows in FY23–FY25.

text: The Centre's fiscal deficit for FY26 has been budgeted at:
explanation:
• The FY26 target is 4.4% of GDP.
  • The deficit was 4.8% of GDP in FY25.
  • Fiscal deficit shows the government's borrowing need.
  • Targets are set under the FRBM Act, 2003.

text: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, the Centre's fiscal deficit in FY25 stood at:
explanation:
• The FY25 fiscal deficit was 4.8% of GDP.
  • It is budgeted to fall to 4.4% in FY26.
  • General government debt-to-GDP fell about 7.1 percentage points since 2020.
  • Three rating upgrades in 2025 credited fiscal prudence.

text: The Centre's revenue deficit budgeted for FY26, the lowest since FY09, is:
explanation:
• The revenue deficit is budgeted at 0.8% of GDP.
  • It is the lowest since FY09.
  • Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts.
  • The fiscal deficit target for FY26 is 4.4%.

text: The number of income tax returns filed in FY25, as per the Economic Survey 2025-26, was:
explanation:
• About 9.2 crore returns were filed in FY25.

  • Centre's revenue receipts rose to 9.2% of GDP in FY25.
  • Direct taxes are now over 58% of total tax revenue.

text: Which central scheme of 50-year interest-free loans helped states keep capital spending near 2.4% of GDP in FY25?
explanation:
• SASCI – Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment.
  • It gives 50-year interest-free loans to states.
  • It began in 2020-21.
  • It kept state capex near 2.4% of GDP in FY25.

text: The new GST rates under 'GST 2.0' came into effect from:
explanation:
• New rates applied from 22 September 2025.

explanation:
• A special rate of 40% applies to sin and luxury goods.

explanation:

  • R&I of Japan upgraded India to BBB+ in September 2025.

text: As noted in the Economic Survey 2025-26, the RBI's policy repo rate in December 2025 stood at:
explanation:
• The repo rate stood at 5.25%.

text: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) was reduced in stages during September–November 2025 to:
explanation:
• The CRR was cut by 100 bps to 3.0%.

text: Which rate is the operating target of the RBI's monetary policy?
explanation:
• The Weighted Average Call Rate (WACR) is the operating target.
  • It stayed slightly below the repo rate in FY26.
  • This showed smooth transmission of rate cuts.
  • The call money market deals in overnight loans between banks.
